title: Algebra of Artinian deformation tests
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $k$ a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the category $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with specified residue field $k$ and local maps inducing the identity on $k$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. $\mathfrak m_A$ is nilpotent for every $A\in\mathcal C_{R,k}$. If $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ are morphisms and $A_2\to A$ is surjective, the ring $P=A_1\times_A A_2=\{(a_1,a_2):a_1|_A=a_2|_A\}$ is Artinian local with residue field $k$, with its canonical $R$-structure, and $P\to A_1$ is surjective. If $A_2\to A$ is a small extension, $P\to A_1$ is a small extension with the same kernel. Every surjection $B\twoheadrightarrow C$ in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ factors as $B=B_n\twoheadrightarrow B_{n-1}\twoheadrightarrow\cdots\twoheadrightarrow B_0\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ with $n\geq0$, each $B_j\to B_{j-1}$ a small extension and $B_0\to C$ an isomorphism in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$; if its kernel is nonzero one may take $B_0=C$ with the identity, so the surjection is itself a composite of $n\geq1$ small extensions, while $n=0$ exactly when it is an isomorphism. If $\mathfrak p=\ker(R\to k)$ and $\Lambda=R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], then $\Lambda$ is Noetherian local, $k$ is finite as a $\Lambda$-module, and extension of the $R$-structure uniquely identifies $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ with $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$; it also identifies their categories of complete Noetherian local algebras with residue field $k$.

proof.text: For every test algebra $B$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] to its Artinian local underlying ring. This gives $\mathfrak m_B^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$, as asserted, and also gives Noetherianness when needed below.

We will use the following elementary reading of [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ideal-length-one-filtration]. For any ideal $J$ in an Artinian local test algebra $B$, take its finite filtration $0=J_0\subset\cdots\subset J_r=J$ with simple nonzero factors $S_i$. The submodule $\mathfrak m_BS_i$ is either zero or $S_i$. The latter would imply $\mathfrak m_B^NS_i=S_i$, contradicting the nilpotence supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent]. Thus every factor is annihilated by $\mathfrak m_B$, hence is a vector space over $B/\mathfrak m_B=k$. The span of any nonzero vector is a nonzero $B$-submodule, so simplicity says that it is all of $S_i$: each factor has $k$-dimension one.

Let $B\twoheadrightarrow C$ be a morphism in the test category and $J$ its kernel. Apply the filtration and the preceding argument to $J$. Since $J\subset\mathfrak m_B$, all quotients $B/J_i$ have residue field $k$ and are local: an element outside $\mathfrak m_B/J_i$ is the image of a unit. They are Artinian because a descending chain of their ideals pulls back to a chain of ideals of $B$. The maps $B/J_{i-1}\twoheadrightarrow B/J_i$ have kernels $J_i/J_{i-1}$, nonzero of $k$-dimension one and annihilated by their source maximal ideals. They are small extensions by [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Their composite is $B\twoheadrightarrow B/J$, followed by the isomorphism $B/J\cong C$ in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ induced by the given map; this is the asserted factorization with $n=r$. If $J\neq0$ then $r\geq1$, and composing the last small extension $B/J_{r-1}\twoheadrightarrow B/J$ with $B/J\cong C$ gives a surjective morphism with the same kernel $J/J_{r-1}$, isomorphically, so it is again a small extension and $B\twoheadrightarrow C$ is a composite of $r$ small extensions. If $J=0$ the given map is an isomorphism and $r=0$; conversely a composite of $n\geq1$ small extensions has nonzero kernel, so $n=0$ exactly for isomorphisms. A non-identity automorphism (for example $\epsilon\mapsto u\epsilon$ on $k[\epsilon]$, $u\neq1$) is not an empty composite, which is why the final isomorphism is kept.

source.place: Tag 06GE (lemma-factor-small-extension), with a simple ideal filtration in place of the two successive refinements.

proof.text: Write $f_i:A_i\to A$ and $P=\{(a_1,a_2):f_1(a_1)=f_2(a_2)\}$. Coordinatewise operations and $r\mapsto(r|_{A_1},r|_{A_2})$ give the ring and its $R$-structure. For each $a_1$, surjectivity of $f_2$ provides $a_2$ over $f_1(a_1)$, so $\pi_1:P\twoheadrightarrow A_1$. The common residue $\rho:P\to k$ is therefore surjective. Its kernel is $\mathfrak n=\{(a_1,a_2)\in P:a_i\in\mathfrak m_{A_i}\}$. If a pair has nonzero residue, both coordinates are units, and their inverses again have equal image in $A$; hence the pair is a unit of $P$. A pair of zero residue cannot be a unit. Thus $\mathfrak n$ is the unique maximal ideal, $P/\mathfrak n=k$, and both projections are local maps inducing the identity on $k$. Finally $\ker\pi_1=\{(0,j):j\in J\}$ for $J=\ker f_2$, and multiplication on this kernel is $(a_1,a_2)(0,j)=(0,a_2j)$.

source.place: Tag 06GH (lemma-fiber-product-CLambda), proof of (1), explicit local-ring and kernel calculation.

proof.text: It remains to prove $P$ Artinian; we do not infer this merely because it is a subring of $A_1\times A_2$. Filter $J=\ker f_2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ideal-length-one-filtration]. Step 2 shows that its factors are copies of the residue module $k$. Each $\{(0,j):j\in J_i\}$ is a $P$-submodule of $\ker\pi_1$, and $P$ acts on each factor through its surjective residue map $P\to k$. Its $P$-submodules are consequently its $k$-subspaces, so each factor has length one. Repeated use of [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] gives finite $P$-length of $\ker\pi_1$. The $P$-submodules of $A_1$ are exactly its $A_1$-ideals since $\pi_1$ is surjective. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ring-self-finite-length] gives finite $P$-length of $A_1$. Apply length additivity to $0\to\ker\pi_1\to P\to A_1\to0$ to obtain finite length of $P$ over itself. A strictly descending chain of ideals would give arbitrarily long finite strict chains, contradicting this finite bound. Hence $P$ is Artinian and is an object of the test category.

If $f_2$ is small, its kernel $J$ is a one-dimensional $k$-vector space annihilated by $\mathfrak m_{A_2}$. The map $j\mapsto(0,j)$ is an additive isomorphism $J\cong\ker\pi_1$. The multiplication formula of step 4 shows that the action on this kernel factors through the same residue field $k$, and $\mathfrak n$ annihilates it because its second coordinate lies in $\mathfrak m_{A_2}$. The kernel is therefore nonzero of $k$-dimension one. Together with surjectivity this says that $\pi_1$ is a small extension by [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category], with its kernel canonically identified with $J$.

Put $\mathfrak p=\ker(R\to k)$, a prime ideal since $k$ is a field, and $\Lambda=R_{\mathfrak p}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. This is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p\Lambda$ and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. For any local $R$-algebra $B$ with specified residue $k$ (Artinian, or complete Noetherian), every $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ has nonzero residue in $B$ and hence is a unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] there is a unique extended structure $\Lambda\to B$, explicitly $r/s\mapsto r_Bs_B^{-1}$. It is local: its composite to $k$ has kernel $\mathfrak p\Lambda$. Any $R$-map between two such $B$ commutes with these extended structures by uniqueness (or by the displayed fraction formula). Conversely any $\Lambda$-map is an $R$-map. Extension and restriction thus identify the test categories, preserving their specified residue identifications. The same construction identifies the complete Noetherian local categories: the underlying rings, maximal ideals, quotient towers and canonical maps to their inverse limits are unchanged, so completeness and Noetherianness are unchanged. Any requirement of maximal-ideal-adic continuity of morphisms is likewise unchanged.

The map $\Lambda\to k$ annihilates $\mathfrak p\Lambda$, so it induces an inclusion of fields $k_0=\Lambda/\mathfrak p\Lambda=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\hookrightarrow k$. Choose finitely many $R$-algebra generators of $k$, using the given finite-type hypothesis. The same elements generate $k$ over $k_0$: the $k_0$-subalgebra they generate contains the image of $R$ and all its generators, hence all of $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] to the field extension $k_0\subset k$ to get $[k:k_0]<\infty$. A $k_0$-basis also generates $k$ as a $\Lambda$-module, since $\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow k_0$ is surjective. Thus $k$ is finite over $\Lambda$, completing the last clause. No assertion that $\mathfrak p$ is maximal in $R$ is needed.
